header.userPrompt:
At the end of a run, report the tool calls that agents were denied permission for, so users can fix their harness settings or instructions.

Why: orca's agents are ordinary harness sessions that load the user's instruction files and MCP servers. Read-only roles run headless with a fixed allowlist, so a user instruction such as "always call mcp__visdom__agents_md first" makes every planner/reviewer turn try a tool that is denied. In one run this happened 14+ times and nobody noticed; the only trace was the debug log.

What to build:
- Detect denied tool calls in agent turns. For claude, the denial comes back as a tool_result like "Claude requested permissions to use mcp__visdom__agents_md, but you haven't granted it yet." Find the equivalent for the other backends (gemini, codex, opencode, pi); where a backend's denial cannot be told apart from other tool errors, say so in the code and skip it.
- Aggregate per tool name: count and the roles that were denied.
- Print a summary near the end of the run (next to the cost summary), e.g.: `denied tool calls: mcp__visdom__agents_md ×14 (planning, review) — allow it in your harness settings, or relax the instruction that requests it`. Print nothing when there were no denials.
- Also log each denial at DEBUG or INFO in the trace log.

Keep the change small; tests for detection and aggregation.

resultJson.description:
At the end of a run, orca reports the tool calls its agents were denied permission for, so the user can fix their harness settings or the instruction that keeps requesting the tool. Orca's agents are ordinary harness sessions: they load the user's CLAUDE.md-style instruction files and MCP servers, but read-only roles (planner, reviewers) run headless under a fixed allowlist. A user instruction like "always call mcp__visdom__agents_md first" then makes every planner/reviewer turn attempt a tool the harness denies. Today that denial is invisible: for claude it arrives as a failed `tool_result` whose text the autonomous drain deliberately swallows, so the only trace is the DEBUG log. One observed run hit this 14+ times.

The change adds one new flow event, `OrcaEvent.ToolDenied`, emitted by the backend-agnostic autonomous drain when it recognises a denial (claude's "requested permissions to use X, but you haven't granted it yet" tool result, and the drain's own auto-deny of an `ApproveTool` request, which is how opencode's `permission.asked` surfaces). A new listener in the flow module aggregates denials per tool name with a count and the set of agents (role agents are named after their role: `planning`, `coding`, `review`), and prints one summary line per denied tool next to the cost summary at the end of the run, nothing when there were none. Each denial is also mirrored into the trace log. Backends whose denial cannot be told apart from an ordinary tool failure (codex sandbox errors, gemini's unverified headless refusal text) or that have no denial at all (pi's `--tools` allowlist removes the tool from the model's set) are documented as skipped in the detector's scaladoc rather than guessed at.

tasks.title: Add OrcaEvent.ToolDenied and wire it through attribution, trace log and terminal
tasks.description:
In `tools/src/main/scala/orca/events/OrcaEvent.scala` add `case ToolDenied(tool: String, agent: Option[String] = None)` with scaladoc: a tool call the harness refused for lack of permission (as opposed to a tool that ran and failed), emitted by the autonomous drain, `agent` stamped by `attributedTo` like `ToolUse`. Extend `OrcaListener.attributedTo` to stamp it and update its scaladoc (now four display events). Add arms to the two exhaustive matches: `LoggingListener` logs at INFO in plain ASCII, e.g. `tool denied ({}): {}` with agent (`?` when absent) and tool; `TerminalEventListener` renders nothing, with a one-line comment that the end-of-run summary reports denials. Nothing emits the event yet, so the build stays green.

Tests: `attributedTo` stamps the agent name onto `ToolDenied` (in the existing OrcaListener/attribution test location under `tools/src/test`, or a new small suite); `TerminalEventListenerTest`: a `ToolDenied` event between `StageStarted`/`StageCompleted` produces no line beyond the stage header.

tasks.title: Detect denials in the autonomous drain (claude tool_result phrase and ApproveTool auto-deny)
tasks.description:
Add `private[orca] object ToolDenial` in `tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/ToolDenial.scala` with `def fromToolResult(content: String): Option[String]` returning the tool name captured from claude's message `Claude requested permissions to use <tool>, but you haven't granted it yet.` (regex, `findFirstMatchIn`, no dependence on the `ok` flag; `None` for anything else). Its scaladoc records, per backend, where a denial is observable and why the others are skipped: claude — this phrase in a `tool_result`; opencode — `permission.asked` becomes `ApproveTool`, auto-denied by the drain; codex — sandbox blocks are the command's own failure output, indistinguishable from a failing command, skipped; gemini — plan-mode refusals arrive as error tool results with no phrase verified in this repo, skipped (record the probe command if a future pin is wanted; if the gemini CLI is installed and a single probe shows a stable phrase, pin it here with a test instead); pi — `--tools` removes unlisted tools from the model's set, nothing to detect. Note interactive turns are deliberately not covered.

In `Conversations.drainAutonomous`: in the `ToolResult` arm, emit `OrcaEvent.ToolDenied(name)` when the detector matches (keep swallowing everything else; update the arm's comment); in the `ApproveTool` arm, emit `OrcaEvent.ToolDenied(toolName)` in addition to the existing `Error` (existing tests pin the Error text; keep it).

Tests: `ToolDenialTest` — extracts the tool name from the claude phrase; returns `None` for an ordinary failed tool output; returns `None` for an unrelated mention of "permissions". `ConversationsTest` — a claude-shaped `ToolResult(None, ok = false, <phrase>)` emits exactly `ToolDenied("mcp__visdom__agents_md")`; a failed `ToolResult` with other content still emits nothing; an auto-denied `ApproveTool` emits `ToolDenied("Bash")` alongside the existing `Error`.

tasks.title: Aggregate denials per tool and print the summary next to the cost summary
tasks.description:
Add `class DeniedToolTracker extends OrcaListener` in `flow/src/main/scala/orca/events/DeniedToolTracker.scala`, modelled on `CostTracker`: an immutable `State` (per tool: count and the set of agent names) in an `AtomicReference`, updated with `updateAndGet` on `OrcaEvent.ToolDenied`, every other event ignored. `summary: String` renders one line per denied tool, sorted by count descending then tool name: `denied tool calls: <tool> ×<n> (<agents, alphabetical>) — allow it in your harness settings, or relax the instruction that requests it`; a denial with no agent name counts but adds no name (omit the parenthetical when the set is empty); empty string when no denial was recorded. `printSummary(): Unit` mirrors `CostTracker.printSummary` (leading newline, only when non-empty). Scaladoc states the thread-safety contract and why the state is an atomic of an immutable value (same contract and pattern as `CostTracker`; an actor or channel would need an owning scope outliving the listener) — also put that rationale in the commit message per the repo's mutable-state rule.

In `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flowEntry.scala`: construct the tracker beside `costTracker`, add it to the `extraListeners` list passed to `runFlow`, and call `printSummary()` right after `costTracker.printSummary()` in the same `finally`.

Tests in `flow/src/test/scala/orca/DeniedToolTrackerTest.scala`: empty summary with no events and with only non-denial events; one tool denied three times by `planning` and `review` renders `×3 (planning, review)` with agents deduplicated and sorted; two tools order by count then name, one line each; a denial without an agent name is counted and rendered without a parenthetical; concurrent `onEvent` calls from forks in a `supervised` scope lose no counts.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules and pipeline

- `tools/` (package `orca.backend`, `orca.events`, `orca.agents`): backend SPI, event types, the autonomous drain. Every other module depends on it.
- `flow/` (`orca.events.CostTracker` etc.): flow-level listeners. `flow/src/main/scala/orca/events/CostTracker.scala` is the model for a summarising listener.
- `runner/`: wiring (`runner/src/main/scala/orca/flowEntry.scala`), trace mirror (`runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/LoggingListener.scala`), terminal renderer (`runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/terminal/TerminalEventListener.scala`).
- `claude/ codex/ gemini/ opencode/ pi/`: one driver per backend. None needs changing for this epic; they are only evidence for the detector's per-backend scaladoc.

Event flow for an autonomous turn: driver parses the CLI wire into `ConversationEvent` (`tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/ConversationEvent.scala`) → `Conversations.drainAutonomous` (`tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/Conversations.scala`, lines ~128-196) maps them to `OrcaEvent`s (`tools/src/main/scala/orca/events/OrcaEvent.scala`) → the listener handed in is `OrcaListener.attributedTo(events, agentName)` (`BaseAgent.scala:109`, `AgentCall.scala:153`), which stamps the agent name onto `ToolUse`/`AssistantMessage`/`Error` → `EventDispatcher` fans out to `TerminalEventListener`, `LoggingListener`, `CostTracker`, `AttemptManifestWriter` and any `extraListeners`.

## Key facts

- `ConversationEvent.ToolResult(toolName: Option[String], ok: Boolean, content: String)`. claude's driver emits `toolName = None` (its `tool_result` block carries only a `tool_use_id`, see `ClaudeConversation.scala:201-210`); codex/gemini/pi/opencode emit `Some(name)`. The drain currently swallows every `ToolResult` (`Conversations.scala:181-186`).
- claude denial shape (the one to detect): a `tool_result` with content `Claude requested permissions to use <tool>, but you haven't granted it yet.` — the tool name is IN the text, so no id→name correlation is needed. Match the phrase with a regex capturing the name, regardless of `ok` (it arrives as `is_error: true`, but the phrase alone is unambiguous). `ClaudeIntegrationTest.scala:115-147` confirms claude in `--print` mode never routes approval over stdin: refusals arrive as failed tool results.
- `ConversationEvent.ApproveTool(toolName, rawInput, respond)`: the drain auto-denies it (`Conversations.scala:149-165`) and emits `OrcaEvent.Error("Denied <tool>: ...")`. This is how opencode's `permission.asked` (`OpencodeConversation.scala:141-148`) and claude's `can_use_tool` control request (`ClaudeConversation.scala:299-312`, only when not in `autoApproves`) reach an autonomous turn. Count these as denials too; keep the existing `Error` emission (tests in `ConversationsTest.scala:243-327` pin its text).
- Other backends, for the detector's scaladoc (say so in code, skip): codex — sandbox blocks surface as the command's own failure output (`CodexConversation.scala:214-221`, `ok = exitCode.contains(0)`), indistinguishable from a failing command; MCP tools are not permission-gated under `exec` with the sandbox flags `CodexArgs.scala` emits. gemini — a disallowed tool under `--approval-mode plan` comes back as `tool_result` with `status: error` (`GeminiConversation.scala:164-177`), but no stable refusal phrase is recorded anywhere in this repo (docs/research and adr/0016 only say plan mode is "unmeasured"); skip unless a one-off probe (`gemini --skip-trust --approval-mode plan --output-format stream-json -p "create a file x"`) shows a stable phrase, in which case pin it with a test. pi — `PiArgs.ReadOnlyTools` drives a `--tools` allowlist, so an unlisted tool is not offered to the model at all; `tool_execution_end` with `isError` is a tool failure, not a denial. opencode — covered by the `ApproveTool` path; tools disabled by config are not offered.
- Agent naming: `RoleAgents.tagged` (`runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/RoleAgents.scala:232-240`) sets the role agent's `name` to the role label (`planning`, `coding`, `review`) and `role` to the cost role. Reviewers get `withName(<reviewer name>)`, the picker `withName(PickerName)`. So the agent name stamped by `attributedTo` is what the summary should show in parentheses; no separate role plumbing is needed. `BaseAgent.quietTextTurn` filters only `AssistantMessage | ToolUse`, so a new event passes through.
- `OrcaEvent` is an enum; `LoggingListener.onEvent` and `TerminalEventListener.onEvent` match it exhaustively with no wildcard (a new case must get an arm in both). `AttemptManifestWriter`, `CostTracker`, `CostResolvingDispatcher` and the test listeners use wildcards. `OrcaEvent.ToolUse(tool, args, agent: Option[String] = None)` is the shape to mirror; `attributedTo`'s scaladoc says "three display events" — update it.
- `OrcaListener` implementations MUST be thread-safe (called from parallel reviewer forks). `CostTracker` holds an immutable `State` case class in an `AtomicReference` and updates with `updateAndGet`; mirror that. Project rule (CLAUDE.md): new `AtomicReference` state needs its rationale recorded in the PR/commit — here: an Ox actor cannot serve a synchronous `onEvent` called from foreign forks without a scope that outlives the listener, and a channel would need an owner; the atomic-of-immutable-state pattern is the one `CostTracker` already uses for exactly this contract.
- Summary printing: `flowEntry.scala:161` builds `costTracker`, passes it in `extraListeners` (line 207) and prints it in the `finally` at line 247 (`costTracker.printSummary()`), after the terminal interaction is closed. `CostTracker.printSummary` prints `"\n" + summary` via `println` only when non-empty. Put the denied-tools listener beside it, in the same list and the same `finally`.
- Trace log: `LoggingListener` logs to slf4j logger `orca.flow` at INFO for steps/caveats and DEBUG for tool use. Messages are plain ASCII (the `×` glyph belongs only in the terminal summary, not in the log line).
- Terminal: per-event rendering of a denial is NOT wanted (14 lines of noise); the terminal arm is silent with a one-line comment pointing at the end-of-run summary. `TerminalEventListenerTest.scala` shows how to render a list of events to a string.
- Interactive turns (`Conversations.withholdInteractiveProse`) are out of scope: a human is present to approve, so a denial there is the user's own decision. Say so in the detector's scaladoc.

## Files to read / change

- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/events/OrcaEvent.scala` — add `ToolDenied(tool: String, agent: Option[String] = None)` with scaladoc (what counts as a denial, where it is emitted, that `agent` is stamped by `attributedTo`); extend `attributedTo`.
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/Conversations.scala` — emit `ToolDenied` in the `ToolResult` arm when the detector matches, and in the `ApproveTool` arm.
- New `tools/src/main/scala/orca/backend/ToolDenial.scala` — `private[orca] object ToolDenial` with `def fromToolResult(content: String): Option[String]` (the denied tool's name) and the per-backend scaladoc above.
- New `flow/src/main/scala/orca/events/DeniedToolTracker.scala` (public, like `CostTracker`): `onEvent`, `summary: String`, `printSummary(): Unit`.
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/LoggingListener.scala`, `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/terminal/TerminalEventListener.scala` — one arm each.
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flowEntry.scala` — register and print.

## Tests and conventions

- munit. Test files: `tools/src/test/scala/orca/backend/ConversationsTest.scala` (has `ScriptedConversation` + `RecordingListener` fixtures; drain tests build a `List[ConversationEvent]` and assert `recorder.events`), `flow/src/test/scala/orca/CostTrackerTest.scala` (model for the tracker test), `runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/terminal/TerminalEventListenerTest.scala`. One scenario per test.
- Run: `sbt "tools/test"`, `sbt "flow/test"`, `sbt "runner/test"` (or `sbt "tools/testOnly orca.backend.ConversationsTest"`); format with `sbt scalafmtAll` before finishing. Plain `sbt`, not `sbt --client`; never `clean`. Build has `-Wunused:all`; keep zero warnings.
- Style: braceless Scala 3, explicit return types on public members, no class-level `var`, immutable collections, scaladoc for contract, `//` for non-obvious why. Comments are present-tense facts; never cite plan/epic labels. No default values on persisted fields (an `OrcaEvent` is not persisted; `ToolUse`'s `agent = None` default is the precedent). Load the `direct-style-scala` skill before writing Scala.
- Summary line format to produce, one line per denied tool, sorted by count descending then name: `denied tool calls: mcp__visdom__agents_md ×14 (planning, review) — allow it in your harness settings, or relax the instruction that requests it`; agent names sorted alphabetically, a denial with no agent name contributes to the count but no name; empty string when nothing was denied.

resultJson.title: Report denied tool calls at end of run
resultJson.body:
## Summary

When agents run as autonomous harness sessions, they load user instruction files like `CLAUDE.md` that may repeatedly request tools the harness hasn't granted. Today those denials are invisible—buried in the debug log. This change surfaces them.

Adds `OrcaEvent.ToolDenied` to track permission refusals, detected in the autonomous drain for Claude's refusal phrase and opencode's `ApproveTool` auto-deny. A new `DeniedToolTracker` listener aggregates denials by tool and agent, then prints a summary at run's end: `denied tool calls: mcp__visdom__agents_md ×14 (planning, review) — allow it in your harness settings, or relax the instruction that requests it`.

## How it works

- **Detection**: `ToolDenial` extracts the tool name from Claude's "requested permissions to use X, but you haven't granted it yet" phrase in failed tool results. Backend-specific scaladoc explains which other backends' denials are observable (opencode via `ApproveTool`), which cannot be detected reliably (codex sandbox errors, gemini plan-mode refusals), and which have no denial at all (pi's `--tools` allowlist).
- **Attribution**: Extended `OrcaListener.attributedTo` to stamp agent names onto the new event, so the summary knows which roles were denied.
- **Aggregation**: `DeniedToolTracker` uses an Ox actor to safely count denials per tool (thread-safe for parallel reviewer forks). Each denial also logs to the trace at INFO.
- **UI**: Terminal listener stays silent (the end-of-run summary is the full report); logging listener emits one line per denial.

## What changed

- New `OrcaEvent.ToolDenied(tool, agent)` case.
- New detector: `ToolDenial.fromToolResult(content): Option[String]`.
- Drain emits denials from failed `ToolResult` and auto-denied `ApproveTool`.
- New `DeniedToolTracker` listener wired into `flowEntry`, prints alongside cost summary.
- Tests for detection, aggregation (including concurrency), attribution, and UI.
